summary: This is a Bozeman-area hospital itemized statement for a same-day (12/24/24) orthopedic surgery involving fixation of the arm/elbow (multiple titanium plates and screws for the humerus and ulna). Total charges are $97,998.00, reduced by a Self-Pay Discount of $19,599.60, leaving a balance of $78,398.40. The bill was handled as self-pay (no insurance payer appears), and the biggest drivers are operating-room time ($33,330 base + increments), anesthesia time (~$11,782), and a large volume of implant hardware and consumable drill bits/plates (tens of thousands of dollars).
topIssues: Operating room time is $28,684 for 202 increment minutes plus a $4,646 base (~$33,330 total, ~$142/minute) — the single largest charge. Request the operative and anesthesia records to confirm actual OR time before paying, and challenge the per-minute rate.

Two distal humerus implant plates at $4,635 each ($9,270) plus a proximal ulna plate at $3,965 — implant hardware is the most negotiable category. Ask the hospital for the manufacturer/supplier invoices for every plate and screw.

Consumable surgical drill bits are charged at very high rates: $2,941 for three 2x140mm bits, $1,158 for one 2.7x80mm bit, $975 for a 3.5x70mm drill, plus others (~$6,500+ in drill bits). Request itemized supplier costs — single-use drill bits at ~$1,000 each are worth disputing.

The same screw type appears twice at different prices — multi-thread lock 3.5mm screws are $1,446 each under code 278C1713S but $1,205 each under code C1713. Ask why identical items are priced inconsistently.

As a self-pay patient you already received a $19,599.60 discount, but the remaining $78,398.40 is still full chargemaster pricing. You have strong leverage to negotiate further — ask for the cash/prompt-pay rate and cite the supplier invoices for all implants and drill bits.

noSurprises.headline: You may have the right to force a federal review of this bill
noSurprises.detail: This looks like a self-pay or uninsured bill. If your provider gave you a written good faith estimate before treatment and this bill came in at least $400.00 higher, you can make an independent reviewer decide a fair price. Upload that estimate and we will check the gap for you.
steps: Find the written good faith estimate you were given before the procedure.
Upload it here — we will compare it against this bill automatically.
If the gap is $400.00 or more, you can file with CMS within 120 days of the bill date.
Never got an estimate? Providers must give uninsured patients one — that itself is worth a complaint.
protections: Your cost cannot increase because you disputed.
They cannot send this bill to collections while the dispute is open — and must stop pursuing you if it is already there.
Late fees are frozen until the dispute is resolved.
They cannot retaliate against you for disputing.
If you settle directly before it ends, they must still cut at least $12.50 off the bill.
